text: After this you can carry a support decision through six explicit analysis steps.

For education only; this is not legal, purchasing, financial or safety advice. Compare delivery alternatives in a traceable order: define the choice, collect reliable facts, identify workable options, select relevant evaluation criteria, assess each option on a common basis, then explain the preferred choice and its trade-offs. Repeat the affected comparison if material constraints or evidence change. Check whether the result still holds when uncertain inputs move within plausible ranges. A preference that reverses needs to be shown as conditional.

items: State the choice that needs to be made. You should see: The comparison has one defined purpose. If not: Narrow or restate an unclear decision.
Collect evidence, constraints and relevant assumptions. You should see: The basis for judging choices is documented. If not: Identify any material evidence still missing.
Form realistic alternatives. You should see: Each option could plausibly achieve the required task. If not: Remove unworkable choices or document what is needed to test them.
Select the requirements that will be used in the comparison. You should see: The evaluation criteria relate to the defined decision. If not: Explain why a proposed test is relevant.
Assess each option under the same suitable criteria. You should see: Results can be compared and trade-offs seen. If not: Revisit inconsistent scope or missing evidence.
Record a preferred option and its rationale. You should see: The recommendation can be traced to the comparison. If not: Document unresolved trade-offs for the decision authority.
Inferred: Two feasible service choices may rank differently when demand doubles. Record the original comparison, change only the demand assumption, and note whether the preferred choice changes.

text: Every options analysis proceeds from a decision question to a documented choice.
Judge all realistic choices against the same relevant tests.
A material change to the problem or available evidence can require a new assessment.
